findings.title: Null taxRate now causes an unhandled NullPointerException
findings.evidence: The method multiplies the subtotal by taxRate without validating it, so a null caller input will fail at runtime instead of being rejected consistently.
findings.recommendation: Validate taxRate at method entry and throw a clear IllegalArgumentException when it is null, or define and document a default such as BigDecimal.ZERO.

findings.title: Null items list or null elements will crash subtotal/totalWithTax
findings.evidence: The code iterates directly over items and dereferences each item without any null checks, so passing a null list or a list containing null will throw NullPointerException in supported Java runtimes.
findings.recommendation: Reject null items lists and null elements explicitly at the start of subtotal, and consider reusing the same validation from totalWithTax before calling subtotal.

findings.title: Negative tax rates are accepted and can reduce totals below subtotal
findings.evidence: There is no guard on taxRate before computing tax, so callers can pass a negative rate and generate a discount-like negative tax even though the API is named totalWithTax.
findings.recommendation: Validate that taxRate is non-negative, and if rates are expected as percentages also enforce an upper bound or document the accepted range clearly.
